speaker: james_burbage
text: God's body, leave the trap. It is sound enough to wait. This chair will not.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the chair is the morning. Where does it fail?

speaker: james_burbage
text: Where a king sits down too hard. Painted to pass for oak and gilt, and the joint under the seat is a liar. It looks like a throne and it folds like a basket.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: I can stop it folding. Two cleats and a wedge, and it will never move again.

speaker: james_burbage
text: And how does the boy get it off, if it will never move again?

speaker: sam_latchet
text: He doesn't. That is the cure. It works if the chair never has to leave the stage.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then it is a fine cure for a chair that lives here, and a bad one for a chair that has to vanish.

speaker: james_burbage
text: By the mass, that is the whole problem. It must go off in a boy's arms. If I make the mend too brave, Sam carries a house instead of a property.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: I will write what you decide. I would rather write a peg than a lecture.

speaker: james_burbage
text: One peg. Dry, and cut to the old hole. Not so thick that the leg swells into a sermon. Turn it over.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Upside down, then. The weak place is easier to see when a throne is humiliating itself.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Giles Allen may have the ground when the lease falls in. He shall not have this peg. The rest of the morning is wood.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Wood I can follow. Show me the hole.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Here. The old wood is dark. The new peg will stand pale in it, and anyone with eyes will see the mend, which is a honesty I can bear in a property and nowhere else.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: If the pale bit shows, the king is sitting on a patched stool.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The paint is there to pass for oak and gilt. The peg is there so he does not sit on the floor. I will take the pale bit.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Drive it. Not with your poetry. With the mallet, and stop when it is home. A second blow is how a man splits a leg he meant to save.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: One blow past snug, and I stop. Sam, keep your fingers off the cheek.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: My fingers are my own. I am only saying the wedge was kinder.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: The wedge stays in your pocket, Sam. The peg is what I am writing.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Write it so a fool cannot sit the glory out of it. Some men sit down as if a chair had offered them a duel.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: chair, mended; not to be sat on by Master Kemp.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is the line. Leave it.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Kemp is not in the yard to argue with a list. He can argue on a Monday when there is a play. Today there is a peg.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: Will he see it, the pale one, if he comes looking for a throne?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He will see a chair that holds. The pale peg is the proof it was weak, and the proof it is not weak now.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: I have written the names I was given. Chair. Mended. Master Kemp, not to sit. I am not adding a trap to a line about a chair.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Do not. The trap can wait until a play needs it. This was a king sitting down too hard, and a boy who has to carry the consequence off.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are done. I am home by eleven. There is a call, and I would rather meet it than a second joint.

speaker: sam_latchet
text: Leave it upside down till the peg is seen. A mended thing should be looked at before it is a throne again.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Leave it. One peg. Pale in the old dark wood. If anyone paints it out before it has dried, I will know the brush.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not paint it. Thank you for the wood. It was a quieter argument than most of mine.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: The list has it. God keep you on the way home.

speaker: james_burbage
text: Home by eleven, he says. Go, before I find another joint and spoil a good peg.
